title: What The Mbira Knows (Chas McIvor)
style: jazz lounge piano bar dry wit spoken word observational 100bpm upright bass brushed snare deadpan baritone male vocal mbira world instruments Zimbabwe Shona philosophy comedy warm
lyrics:
[Verse 1]
The mbira is made from metal keys and a wooden board
And a calabash gourd for resonance
The gourd is the part most people miss
The music lives inside the hollow space
Not in the key — in what the key disturbs

[Verse 2]
You play it with your thumbs
Which means the mbira trusts your thumbs
With the entire ancestral tradition of the Shona people
Most instruments are less specific about which finger

[Chorus]
What the mbira knows
Lives in the hollow under the note
What the mbira knows
Is carried in the gourd and the throat
The thumbs find the tine, the tine finds the air
What the mbira knows — the mbira puts it there

[Bridge]
Chas was shown a mbira once by Kerri's father Jeff
He held it for a moment without playing it
Then said — it's warm
Jeff said — yes
Chas said — the wood is warm, or the metal?
Jeff said — both
Then Jeff played it
And Chas said — oh
That kind of warm

[Verse 3]
The mbira plays at ceremonies
The mbira plays at crossings
The moment when the farm becomes the airport
The airport becomes the new country
The new country becomes the new home
The mbira knows all of these are the same crossing

[Outro]
What the mbira knows
What the mbira knows
The hollow holds the sound
What the mbira knows
That's my boy
